title: Serre's criterion for affineness
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Assume that $X$ is quasi-compact, that $X$ is
quasi-separated, and that $\mathrm H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ of
finite type. Then $X$ is affine.
(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.3.2, Tag
[01XG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XG).*)

proof.text: For each quasi-coherent ideal I and each first cohomology class x, use the finite-type representative theorem to choose K, its finite-type proof, an inclusion f, and y with H1(f)(y)=x. By the vanishing hypothesis H1(K) is a zero module and hence a subsingleton; y=0. The linear map H1(f) sends zero to zero, so x=0. Thus H1(I) is a subsingleton.

proof.text: Apply quasiCompact_affine_of_h1_ideal_zero to this subsingleton statement for every quasi-coherent ideal. The required QuasiCompact identity-morphism instance follows from CompactSpace X and QuasiSeparatedSpace X. This concludes IsAffine X.
